title: Leg Circles 3 | Bridge
imagery: Imagine you are a hyena laughing at all the other stupid aimals who have come to drink at the oasis

title: Wall Roll Down
works: Works your abdominals and spinal support muscles
imagery: Imagine peeling your spine off the wall one bead at a time
breath: Exhale as the leg slides away, inhale to return
tips: Keep the ribs soft and pelvis steady.
caution: Reduce the range if your back starts to arch.

title: Heel Slides
works: Works your lower abdominals and hip stabilizers
benefits: Improves pelvic control and core coordination
imagery: Imagine your heel is gliding across ice
movement: Hold the bridge and gently lift one foot at a time
breath: Inhale to prepare, exhale for each foot lift
tips: Keep both sides of the pelvis level.
caution: Lower out if you feel strain in your lower back.

title: Bridge March
works: Works your glutes, hamstrings, and core stabilizers
benefits: Improves pelvic stability and single-leg control
imagery: Imagine balancing a tray across your hips
movement: Lift the top leg up and lower with control
breath: Exhale to lift, inhale to lower
tips: Keep the leg slightly turned in to target the outer hip.
caution: Do not let the torso roll backward.

title: Side-Lying Leg Lift
works: Works your outer hips and waist stabilizers
benefits: Builds hip strength and pelvic control
imagery: Imagine your top leg reaching long through the heel
movement: Hold a long straight line from head to heels
breath: Breathe steadily and widen the back of the ribs
tips: Draw the belly in gently and keep the neck relaxed.
caution: Step closer to the wall if your wrists or shoulders feel overloaded.

title: Wall Plank
works: Works your shoulders, core, and chest support muscles
benefits: Improves posture, core endurance, and shoulder stability
imagery: Imagine pressing the wall away while growing taller
movement: Rotate from the waist to one side, return to center, then switch
breath: Exhale to twist, inhale to come back through center
tips: Keep both sitting bones grounded as you turn.
caution: Keep the twist gentle if you have back sensitivity.

title: Seated Spine Twist
works: Works your obliques and postural muscles
benefits: Improves rotational mobility and upright posture
imagery: Imagine your spine spiraling upward like a tall ribbon
placement: Rotate from the waist to one side, return to center, then switch
movement: Exhale to twist, inhale to come back through center
breath: Keep both sitting bones grounded as you turn.
tips: Keep the twist gentle if you have back sensitivity.
